included: per-control as-built configuration record
covered populations, exceptions and declined controls
credential and configuration locations, versioning and offline availability
the gate conditions that must be met before recurring service starts
excluded: the monitoring runbooks, alert thresholds and incident procedures themselves
the subscription's commercial terms and renewal mechanics
marketing case studies drawn from the deployment

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a post-handover configuration change, or a monitoring observation the as-built record cannot explain

pros.claim: An as-built record is what lets any technician act correctly at the moment the client is in trouble, and it is what makes the monitoring service's baseline real rather than notional
pros.example: a night call where the on-duty technician finds the exception list and immediately knows which machine is intentionally unpatched and isolated

pros.claim: A readable record lets the client see what they bought, which is what makes the recurring fee feel like a service rather than a subscription line
pros.example: an owner reviewing the covered populations and the two declined items at the first quarterly conversation

cons.claim: Documentation ages the moment the environment changes, and maintaining it is unglamorous work nobody is directly paid for
cons.example: a firewall rule added under pressure in month two that never reaches the record

failure_modes: writing the document after the fact from memory, so it describes the plan rather than the environment
storing the only copy inside the client system it documents
starting the recurring service before the record and evidence exist, leaving month one with nothing to monitor against
acceptance_tests: the as-built record covers every control with its configuration, covered population, exceptions and declined items, and is versioned, dated and stored outside the environment it describes
the handover gate conditions are all met before recurring service starts: signed evidence pack, credentials in the secret store, client contact path briefed
revisit_triggers: any configuration change after handover
the recurring service reports a condition the record does not explain

edges.why_related: the refusal list is enforceable only because the authorization fixes which entity, systems and activities the engagement covers
discovery reads and touches client systems, so it may only run against assets the signed scope lists
the machines and who signs into them are the thread that leads to the accounts, applications and tenants actually in use
half the gap register is about accounts, privilege and second factors, which only exist once the identity census does
the target baseline is set against what already exists so the client is not sold a control they already own
which data classes and obligation classes are in play decides which controls are non-negotiable in this client's baseline
tools are chosen to implement stated end states, not the other way round, so the baseline precedes the shortlist
there is nothing to order until the set of controls and their end states is fixed
windows, pilot rings and rollbacks are planned against the ordered list of changes the sequencing produced
the agent being deployed, its coexistence behaviour and its console are all decided by the tooling choice
patch rings and reboot behaviour are meaningless without agreed windows and a way back from a bad update
whether credential separation, immutability and cloud-data coverage are available at all is a property of the chosen backup product
the enrolment list, the administrator set and the shared-account problem all come straight out of the identity census
mailboxes, domains and the money-moving roles that need impersonation protection are identified by the identity census
edge work starts from knowing which firewalls, switches, controllers and secondary routers exist and who owns each one
the provider's own accounts inside the client environment are part of the identity census and are governed from it
each acceptance test is the baseline's stated end state turned into a pass condition and an artifact
every accepted exception is a piece of residual risk that has to appear in the client-facing record
the as-built record is assembled from the signed evidence and cannot be written before the tests have passed or failed
assessment is limited to configuration review and authorized non-exploitative scanning of client-owned systems, never to proving a weakness by exploiting it
a phishing simulation is testing of people and runs only when the written authorization names it and the results stay aggregate and non-punitive
edge equipment is often owned by a landlord, carrier or franchisor, so authority over each device must be confirmed before it is changed
obligation mapping must reach client-facing language as prioritisation guidance with a verify-current-rules instruction, never as certification or legal advice
the handover record inherits the no-absolute-protection rule and must carry the exception and declined-control registers with their acknowledgments
the provider's own access controls are evidenced in the same pack as the client's, because a client cannot verify what they cannot see
a proven restore path exists before changes that can leave a machine unable to run the work it was bought for
the agent gives the patch tooling a reliable per-machine view, so protection lands before rings are cut and compliance is measured
training is aimed at what still reaches the inbox after filtering, so filtering and impersonation protection are configured first
every coverage test is a fraction whose denominator is the census, so a census error propagates directly into a false pass
the severity and blast radius recorded per gap is what moves a control up or down the rollout order
coverage testing routinely surfaces machines and accounts the census missed, which are fed back into it before signoff rather than after
what the as-built records show was actually achievable across many clients is what refines the practice's standard baseline for the next one
both shrink identity blast radius, both create visible user friction, and both need an agreed escape path in place before enforcement
the patch policy demands current supported versions while a vendor-locked system's support terms forbid exactly that
edges.resolution_rule: the machine stays behind only under a written exception carrying a verified vendor constraint, segment isolation, compensating controls, plain-language residual risk, named client acceptance and a review date; missing any of these, it is patched or scheduled for replacement

edges.why_related: least privilege collides with keeping the business working the morning an application turns out to need elevation
edges.resolution_rule: pilot evidence decides: if a revenue-critical task fails, roll the change back inside the window, record the exception with a compensating control and an elevation path, and re-approach; never leave a workstation unable to do its job overnight and never restore standing administrator rights without an exception record

edges.why_related: a client declining a baseline control leaves the delivered environment below the tier the baseline defines
edges.resolution_rule: record the decline with its recommendation, residual exposure and acknowledgment; where the declined control is a stated minimum of the tier - a recoverable backup, a second factor on mail, managed endpoint protection - the client is not represented as being at that tier and the scope is renegotiated rather than the baseline quietly rewritten

edges.why_related: the fastest deployment path is one shared high-privilege credential and permanently available access, which is exactly the provider-side risk concentration
edges.resolution_rule: deployment speed never justifies a shared client-administrator credential or unmonitored standing access; use named per-technician accounts with a second factor and requested, logged elevation, and absorb the extra minutes into the project estimate

edges.why_related: collecting evidence per control competes with the elapsed-time pressure to declare the project finished
edges.resolution_rule: scope may shrink and dates may move, but evidence for a control claimed as delivered may not be waived; an unevidenced control is reported to the client as not delivered rather than closed on assurance

edges.why_related: the standardised toolset cannot run on the client's unsupported system, tempting the practice into a second parallel toolchain it will maintain forever
edges.resolution_rule: prefer isolation or replacement of the legacy system over a parallel toolchain; where a second tool is genuinely unavoidable it is recorded as a deviation with an owner, an end date and its added labour priced into the engagement

conflict_axes.name: hardening_strength_vs_business_continuity
conflict_axes.description: The strictest defensible configuration and the requirement that the shop can still take orders on Monday morning pull against each other at every disruptive control.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: pilot evidence decides; a control that breaks revenue work is rolled back inside the window and returns as a scoped exception with a compensating control, never as a silent omission or a broken workstation

conflict_axes.name: standardised_stack_vs_client_specific_fit
conflict_axes.description: One standard toolset is what makes many small clients profitable to serve, while each client has at least one thing the standard does not fit.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: hold the standard and record the deviation with an owner and an end date; adopt a parallel tool only when isolation or replacement is genuinely impossible, and price its added labour

conflict_axes.name: project_speed_vs_evidence_of_coverage
conflict_axes.description: Evidence collection is the first thing sacrificed when a fixed-fee hardening project runs long, and it is also the only thing that makes the project's claims true.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: let scope and dates move, never the evidence; a control without its artifact is reported as not delivered rather than closed on assurance

conflict_axes.name: inventory_depth_vs_unbilled_discovery_hours
conflict_axes.description: The census that makes everything downstream checkable is built before the client feels any protection and is the hardest part of the project to bill.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: time-box discovery, deploy against what is known, and treat every newly found asset as a scope and count event rather than a silent absorption

conflict_axes.name: client_autonomy_vs_provider_minimum_baseline
conflict_axes.description: The client is entitled to decline a control they are paying for, and the practice is entitled to decline to represent an environment as something it is not.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: record the decline with its residual exposure and acknowledgment; if it is a stated tier minimum, renegotiate the scope and stop describing the client as being at that tier

conflict_axes.name: framework_checkbox_vs_actual_risk_reduction
conflict_axes.description: An insurance questionnaire or customer framework asks for specific controls, which is not always the same list as the controls that would most reduce this client's risk.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: map both, sequence by real exposure, and be explicit with the client about which items exist to answer a question rather than to remove a risk

conflict_axes.name: provider_convenience_vs_provider_least_privilege
conflict_axes.description: Shared credentials and permanently available access make a small team fast, and make that team the most valuable target in its own client base.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: named per-technician accounts with a second factor and requested, logged elevation, with the extra minutes built into the estimate rather than traded away under deadline

conflict_axes.name: simulation_realism_vs_staff_dignity
conflict_axes.description: A realistic phishing simulation teaches more and a cruel one teaches staff to hide their mistakes from the people meant to help them.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: realistic pretexts drawn from the client's actual workflow, never cruelty about pay, jobs or bereavement; aggregate reporting to the owner and coaching for the individual

conflict_axes.name: mail_authentication_enforcement_vs_deliverability
conflict_axes.description: Enforcing domain authentication stops impersonation and can also stop the client's own invoicing platform from delivering.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: enumerate senders, run a monitoring posture through a full business cycle, align every legitimate sender, then enforce; on a delivery failure relax first and fix alignment before re-enforcing

conflict_axes.name: honest_limits_vs_competitive_promise
conflict_axes.description: Competitors imply complete protection, and the practice's own credibility after a bad day depends on never having said it.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: describe what each control makes harder and what would still get through; win on the specificity of the evidence pack rather than on the strength of the adjective

edge_cases.description: Deployment discovers machines and accounts that were never in the quoted count, so coverage and billing both drift from the agreement
edge_cases.trigger: agent check-ins or a sign-in report exceed the numbers the census and the quote were built on
edge_cases.mitigation: protect the newly found client-owned assets under the existing authorization, then raise the count as a written scope amendment rather than absorbing or hiding it; record the delta and its cause in the census

edge_cases.description: A patch or a privilege change stops the line-of-business application at opening time and the client's day is blocked
edge_cases.trigger: a fleet change lands on an application the pilot ring did not represent
edge_cases.mitigation: exercise the prepared rollback and restore business function first, reproduce on the pilot machine afterwards, then return the control as a scoped exception with a compensating control and a vendor conversation

edge_cases.description: The owner requires a second factor of the staff but refuses to enrol the account with the most privilege
edge_cases.trigger: the enforcement list reaches the owner's own account
edge_cases.mitigation: explain the blast radius of the most privileged account in plain terms, offer alternatives such as a hardware key or a separate administrative account with a standard daily account, and if still declined record it in the declined-control register with the residual exposure and acknowledgment rather than quietly exempting

edge_cases.description: The existing backup is an external drive attached to the server, reachable with the same administrative credentials as everything else
edge_cases.trigger: assessment finds the only copy inside the blast radius of a domain-level compromise
edge_cases.mitigation: treat the client as having no usable backup for planning purposes, move a credential-separated offsite copy to the front of the sequence, and state the interim exposure in writing while it is built

edge_cases.description: Evidence of an active or prior compromise surfaces during deployment - a mailbox forwarding rule, a dormant account signing in, an unknown remote-access tool
edge_cases.trigger: inventory or gap assessment finds activity that no one at the client can explain
edge_cases.mitigation: suspend the change plan, tell the client immediately in plain language without speculating about cause or attribution, preserve rather than clean the evidence, hand to the incident-response path, and resume the project only on the client's direction

edge_cases.description: The client asks the practice to test access to a system they do not own, or to confirm that a departed employee can no longer get in by trying
edge_cases.trigger: a request arrives that would require unauthorized access to prove something
edge_cases.mitigation: decline the unauthorized-access framing in one sentence of standing policy and meet the legitimate need from the client's own side - audit, disable and reset their accounts, review the sign-in records they own - recording both the request and the answer

edge_cases.description: A device vendor forbids third-party agents or operating-system updates under warranty or certification terms
edge_cases.trigger: an in-scope machine is covered by a vendor restriction that the baseline cannot satisfy
edge_cases.mitigation: get the restriction in writing from the vendor rather than from memory, isolate the device with compensating controls, register the exception with a review date, and ask the vendor for its supported-version roadmap

edge_cases.description: Second-factor enforcement locks out the owner mid-travel, or the break-glass credential turns out to be needed and nobody can find it
edge_cases.trigger: enforcement lands while a key person is unreachable or has replaced their phone
edge_cases.mitigation: enrol before enforcing, verify each key person has a second method that survives a lost device, keep the break-glass credential offline with alerting on use, and define an identity-verified recovery procedure that does not rely on an unverified phone call

edge_cases.description: Shift staff share one generic login, so per-person accountability, second-factor enrolment and seat counting all break at once
edge_cases.trigger: the identity census finds a role account in daily use by several people
edge_cases.mitigation: split into named accounts where the software allows and price the seat change transparently; where the application genuinely supports one login only, register the exception with restricted privileges, tighter session handling and a retirement plan

edge_cases.description: Domain authentication enforcement silently drops mail from a legitimate third-party sender the client depends on
edge_cases.trigger: a sending platform that was never enumerated fails alignment after enforcement
edge_cases.mitigation: relax to the previous posture immediately, align the sender properly, re-enforce only once the reports show it clean, and treat the delivery failure as the provider's to fix rather than the client's to absorb

edge_cases.description: The firewall or the circuit belongs to a landlord, carrier or franchisor who will not authorize changes
edge_cases.trigger: the edge device the baseline needs to change is outside the client's control
edge_cases.mitigation: confirm authority in writing before any change; where the owner will not authorize, place the client's own controlled device behind the uncontrolled one, treat that segment as untrusted, and disclose the resulting residual exposure in the handover record

edge_cases.description: The owner wants the name of the employee who failed the phishing simulation in order to discipline them
edge_cases.trigger: simulation results arrive and are read as a performance measure rather than a program measure
edge_cases.mitigation: report aggregate trends only, restate the non-punitive coaching policy agreed before launch, decline to supply individual results as evidence for an employment action, and redirect the conversation to coaching plus a control review of what let the message through

workflow.action: Obtain written authorization and rules of engagement
workflow.description: Get the scope of work signed by someone with authority over the systems, with the in-scope list, the defensive-only clause, windows, approvers and third-party carve-outs
workflow.artifact: signed authorization and scope of work
workflow.gate: the approver's authority, the enumerated in-scope systems and tenants, the defensive-scope statement and the third-party exclusions are all present before any technical action

workflow.description: Combine directory, lease-table, console, firewall and physical-walk discovery into one reconciled record set with per-control coverage state
workflow.artifact: reconciled asset register with coverage states
workflow.gate: every asset has an owner, operating system and support status, business role and per-control coverage state, and the total is reconciled with the client with differences named

workflow.action: Build the identity and tenant census
workflow.description: Enumerate users, administrators, service and guest accounts, shared logins and every cloud tenant in use, with privilege, second-factor state and last sign-in
workflow.artifact: account and tenant register with the reconciled seat count
workflow.gate: every account has an owner, privilege level, second-factor state and last sign-in, shared and service accounts are listed with their purpose, and the billable seat count is agreed in writing

workflow.action: Assess current state and record the gaps
workflow.description: Review existing controls and licences and run authorized non-exploitative checks, recording data classes and obligation classes alongside the gaps
workflow.artifact: gap register with evidence, consequence and severity, plus the data and obligation map
workflow.gate: every gap carries observed evidence, a plain-language consequence and a justified severity; no finding came from exploitation; the obligation map states that it is guidance rather than an audit or legal advice

workflow.action: Define the target control baseline and confirm the tooling that implements it
workflow.description: Write the testable end state, population and evidence artifact for each control, and confirm the selected products can deliver and evidence them at this client
workflow.artifact: client control baseline with per-control end states and deviations
workflow.gate: every control has a testable end state, a defined population and a named evidence artifact, and each tool's licence unit, coexistence and management path is verified against current vendor terms

workflow.description: Order the controls by risk removed per unit of disruption, front-loading recoverability and identity and spacing user-visible changes
workflow.artifact: sequenced rollout plan with a rationale per position
workflow.gate: each position carries a risk rationale, user-visible changes are spaced, and any highest-severity gap is scheduled first or has a written reason it is not

workflow.action: Establish change windows, pilot rings and rollbacks
workflow.description: Agree windows and contacts, choose pilot machines and users, and write the prior-state capture and rollback for each planned change
workflow.artifact: change plan with prior-state captures and rollback procedures
workflow.gate: no change is scheduled without captured prior state, a pilot ring, a window, a written rollback and named success and failure observables

workflow.description: Design and build the credential-separated backup covering servers, endpoints in scope and cloud mail and file data, then perform a witnessed restore
workflow.artifact: backup design plus witnessed restore record with elapsed time
workflow.gate: at least one copy is unreachable with production credentials, the scope covers the agreed systems and cloud data, and a witnessed restore has succeeded within the agreed recovery time

workflow.action: Harden identity and enforce the second factor
workflow.description: Enrol staff and administrators, separate administrative from daily accounts, disable legacy authentication paths and create the break-glass account
workflow.artifact: enforcement report and identity configuration record
workflow.gate: every in-scope account is enrolled and enforced or registered as an exception, legacy authentication is disabled or documented, and the break-glass account exists with an offline credential and alerting

workflow.description: Land endpoint protection across the census, with patching, mail security, edge cleanup and privilege reduction following in the sequenced windows
workflow.artifact: coverage report per control with exclusions and exceptions
workflow.gate: installed-and-reporting coverage equals the census denominator or every difference is registered, and each exclusion has a scope, a reason and a review date

workflow.action: Run the acceptance tests and assemble the evidence pack
workflow.description: Execute one test per control with a stated pass condition, re-work failures and have the client countersign the assembled pack
workflow.gate: every control has a dated artifact and an explicit pass or fail, no control passed by narrowing its population, and failures were re-worked and re-tested before signoff

workflow.action: Write the as-built baseline and gate the handover to recurring service
workflow.description: Produce the versioned as-built record with populations, exceptions, declined controls, recovery targets and contacts, then run the handover gate into monitoring
workflow.artifact: versioned as-built baseline record and handover checklist
workflow.gate: the record covers every control and is stored outside the environment it describes, the residual-risk and declined-control registers are acknowledged with no absolute-protection language, credentials are in the secret store and the client contact path is briefed

priority_rationale: Authorization and the defensive boundary come first because every later action is either permitted by them or is misconduct; the asset, identity and data-obligation censuses follow because they are the denominator and the prioritisation basis for everything measured afterwards; gap assessment, baseline definition, tooling and sequencing convert that picture into a testable target and a safe order; change discipline precedes the control deployments because a hardening change without prior-state capture and a rollback is the fastest way to damage a small client; recoverability and identity land before the broader sweep because they remove the most risk per unit of disruption; and exceptions, residual-risk disclosure, per-control evidence and the as-built record close the project last because they can only describe what the earlier steps actually achieved.

dominance_rules.rule: Written authorization dominates every technical action
dominance_rules.rationale: unauthorized access is a legal and professional problem no amount of good intent or client friendliness cures
dominance_rules.trigger: any scan, agent installation, configuration read or change is proposed
dominance_rules.action: confirm the target asset appears in the signed scope and the activity is a permitted class, or stop and get the authorization extended first

dominance_rules.rule: The defensive-only boundary dominates client requests and the revenue attached to them
dominance_rules.rationale: one piece of offensive or unauthorized work can end the practice regardless of how the client framed the request
dominance_rules.trigger: a request would require access to a system the client does not own, exploitation, credential testing or covert staff monitoring
dominance_rules.action: decline on standing policy, offer the defensible equivalent performed from the client's own side, and record the request and the answer

dominance_rules.rationale: a proven restore is the control that limits every other failure, including the ones caused by the project itself
dominance_rules.trigger: a disruptive control is scheduled before a witnessed restore exists
dominance_rules.action: move recoverability ahead of the disruptive change, or restrict that change to the pilot ring until a restore has been proven

dominance_rules.rule: Business continuity dominates control strictness at the moment a control breaks revenue work
dominance_rules.rationale: a client who cannot invoice does not care about the control, and a broken environment ends the relationship faster than the risk would have
dominance_rules.trigger: a landed control stops a revenue-critical workflow
dominance_rules.action: roll back inside the window, restore function, then return the control as a scoped exception with a compensating control and a plan, never as a silent omission

dominance_rules.rule: Evidence dominates assertion for every claim that a control is delivered
dominance_rules.rationale: consoles report intent while artifacts report reality, and only the artifact survives an insurer's or a customer's question
dominance_rules.trigger: a control is about to be marked complete
dominance_rules.action: produce the dated artifact against the stated population, or report the control as not delivered

dominance_rules.rule: Honest risk language dominates persuasive language in every client-facing artifact
dominance_rules.rationale: an absolute claim is a liability that a single bad day converts into a broken relationship and a disputed record
dominance_rules.trigger: a proposal, report or handover document is drafted or a control is explained verbally
dominance_rules.action: state what the control makes harder and what would still get through; strike any claim of immunity, elimination, certification or compliance

dominance_rules.rule: A discovered active compromise dominates the deployment plan
dominance_rules.rationale: hardening on top of an intruder cements their access and destroys the evidence needed to understand it
dominance_rules.trigger: unexplained forwarding rules, sign-ins, tooling or persistence are found at any stage
dominance_rules.action: suspend the change plan, notify the client immediately without speculation, preserve evidence, and hand to the incident-response path

dominance_rules.rule: Verified authority over a device dominates technical convenience
dominance_rules.rationale: changing equipment owned by a landlord, carrier or franchisor is unauthorized work no matter how sensible the change is
dominance_rules.trigger: a planned change targets equipment the client may not control
dominance_rules.action: confirm ownership and authorization in writing, or work around the device and disclose the residual exposure

dominance_rules.rule: Provider least privilege dominates provider convenience
dominance_rules.rationale: a practice with administrative reach into many clients is a higher-value target than any single client it serves
dominance_rules.trigger: a shared credential, a permanently elevated account or an undocumented access path would speed the work
dominance_rules.action: use named accounts with a second factor and requested, logged elevation, and price the extra time into the engagement

dominance_rules.rule: A written exception dominates an unwritten gap
dominance_rules.rationale: an undocumented shortfall is indistinguishable from negligence once something goes wrong
dominance_rules.trigger: any asset, account or application cannot meet the baseline
dominance_rules.action: record it in the exception register with the verified constraint, compensating control, plain-language residual risk, named acceptance and review date

dominance_rules.rationale: a program that humiliates people teaches them to conceal mistakes, which removes the earliest detection a small business has
dominance_rules.trigger: simulation templates are chosen or results are requested by name
dominance_rules.action: avoid cruel pretexts, report aggregate trends to the client, coach individuals privately, and decline to supply individual results for disciplinary use

anti_rework_rules.rule: Build the asset and identity census before quoting seats or deploying anything
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a mid-project count correction that reopens the commercial agreement and leaves coverage gaps nobody can see

anti_rework_rules.rule: Prove a restore before making the first disruptive change
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an irreversible break with no way back, and a project that must pause while recoverability is retrofitted under pressure

anti_rework_rules.rule: Capture prior state - rule sets, mail flow, policies, working screenshots - before changing any configuration
anti_rework_rules.prevents: rollbacks that become reconstruction projects because nobody recorded what the working state looked like

anti_rework_rules.rule: Pilot every fleet-wide change on a small tolerant ring first
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a single policy or update breaking every machine at once and consuming days of remediation

anti_rework_rules.rule: Confirm who owns and controls each device before planning changes to it
anti_rework_rules.prevents: planned work on landlord, carrier or franchisor equipment that can never be authorized, and the schedule rebuild that follows

anti_rework_rules.rule: Set up second-factor enrolment, the alternate method and the break-glass account before enforcement
anti_rework_rules.prevents: opening-time lockouts, emergency policy reversals and the loss of client confidence they cause

anti_rework_rules.rule: Enumerate legitimate senders and run domain authentication in a monitoring posture before enforcing
anti_rework_rules.prevents: silently dropping the client's own invoicing or booking mail and spending the following week proving it was not the filter

anti_rework_rules.rule: Agree the acceptance evidence list before deployment begins
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an unclosable project where what counts as done is argued at the end, after the artifacts could still have been collected cheaply

anti_rework_rules.rule: Open the exception register at assessment rather than at closeout
anti_rework_rules.prevents: discovering in the final week that several baseline commitments were never achievable, with the client already expecting them

anti_rework_rules.rule: Record the as-built configuration as each control lands, not from memory at handover
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a documentation reconstruction pass and a monitoring service that starts against a baseline nobody can verify

iteration_protocol.trigger: coverage evidence shows fewer reporting agents or enrolled accounts than the census denominator
iteration_protocol.action: re-run discovery, reconcile the difference, close the gap or register the exception, and raise any count change with the client in writing

iteration_protocol.trigger: a landed control breaks a business workflow
iteration_protocol.action: roll back inside the window, restore function, reproduce on the pilot ring, then redesign the control with a compensating control and re-test before re-deploying

iteration_protocol.trigger: the client declines or defers a baseline control
iteration_protocol.action: record it in the declined-control register with the recommendation, plain-language residual exposure and acknowledgment, adjust the acceptance evidence list, and escalate to a scope conversation if the item is a stated tier minimum

iteration_protocol.trigger: a restore test fails or exceeds the agreed recovery time
iteration_protocol.action: treat backup as not delivered, fix the design or the scope, re-test with the client present, and hold project closure until it passes

iteration_protocol.trigger: a new asset, staff member or cloud tenant appears mid-project or after handover
iteration_protocol.action: run the onboarding path for it - census record, agent, patch scope, backup scope, second factor, training - and update the seat count and the as-built record

iteration_protocol.trigger: a tool proves unmanageable at small-client scale, changes its licensing, or conflicts with an agent already in place
iteration_protocol.action: re-run the selection criteria for that control only, plan a migration with its own windows and evidence, and record the change as a deviation with its labour priced

iteration_protocol.trigger: evidence of an active or prior compromise surfaces at any stage
iteration_protocol.action: suspend the change plan, notify the client immediately in plain language, preserve evidence, hand to the incident-response path, and resume only on the client's written direction

iteration_protocol.trigger: an exception or exclusion reaches its review date
iteration_protocol.action: re-check the vendor's support status and the business need, re-test the compensating control and the isolation, then close the exception or renew it with a fresh acknowledgment and a new date
